habitat: Singly, in pairs or in family groups at lakes, dams, large rivers, sewage works, lagoons and estuaries. It enters suburbia only in the north of its distribution.
summary: A common resident. Strikingly black and white, with a tail about the length of a Cape Wagtail’s. In the female and juvenile the male’s black areas are dark brown or grey. The call is a loud tu-weee and twee-twee-twee. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

calls.description: A loud tu-weee and twee-twee-twee. Grade A call from near Richards Bay, KwaZulu-Natal. The filename is XC620809-5 Good P Wagtail.mp3. A Kruger recording of this species on xeno-canto is under a no-derivatives licence and was not used.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Black and white are not split into separate tokens where Newman only says black-and-white. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Cape Wagtail is greyish, with a white throat and a black breast-band, not a black-and-white bird. Newman says the tail lengths are similar.
